title: Active-active traffic divergence and backpressure strategy for streaming sessions
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
Redwood's hosted API must maintain latency and availability SLOs during multi-region incidents while supporting long-lived streaming sessions. Current active-active steering can cause abrupt session disruption, duplicate downstream state, and KV cache divergence when traffic is shifted quickly between regions. Client-side reconnects and model state resets have caused observed SLO breaches in previous incidents.

Goal:
Design and implement a traffic divergence and backpressure strategy at the edge/gateway that preserves streaming session continuity where possible, provides graceful handoff semantics for in-flight streams, and enforces circuit breakers and load-shedding policies to protect tail latency SLOs under region degradation. The solution should be feature-flagged and rollout-safe for runtime-1.22.

Proposal overview (high level):
1) Session-aware divergence controller: augment gateway steering to include per-session affinity tokens and a short-lived handoff token that encodes KV-cache version and last-acknowledged offset. When shifting weight between regions, the controller will attempt a streamed handshake so the new region can warm a hot-path before killing the old stream.

2) Streaming handshake protocol: implement a 3-way soft-handoff on the proxy layer: a) probe -> replica warms caches and confirms capability, b) continued dual-feed mode (both regions receive the same token stream for 250-500ms) for overlapping in-flight tokens, c) commit -> old region drains and connection is trimmed. This preserves continuity for interactive clients with modest additional cost.

3) Backpressure and per-path queueing: gateways enforce dynamic per-connection token admission using real-time queue depth and per-request latency budgets. When queues exceed thresholds, gateway applies backpressure to upstream throttles and signals clients via structured gRPC/HTTP frames.

4) Circuit breakers & tiered load-shedding: add multi-dimensional circuit breakers that trigger by region health, kernel saturation, token tail-latency, and model-variant error rates. Load-shedding policies by customer tier: P0/P1 customers get preferential queuing and lower-shedding thresholds; free-tier and lower-priority requests are subject to early drop and degraded-model fallback.

5) KV-cache reconciliation strategy: avoid aggressive synchronous KV-syncs across regions. Instead use speculative warming + eventual reconciliation. For deterministic state (prefix caches), use warmup tokens during divergence; for mutable ephemeral state, accept best-effort continuity and present clear client-level retry signals.

6) Observability and SLOs: add new telemetry (per-session failover latency, handoff success rate, dual-feed duration, drop-rate by tier). Define SLOs: 99.9% of streaming requests maintain continuity across a planned shift under normal load; under degraded conditions, tail latency SLO (99.9) must be preserved by shedding lower-tier traffic.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Dual-feed overlap increases cost and inter-region bandwidth but reduces client-visible errors for interactive streams.
- Strong synchronous KV replication would guarantee continuity but adds unacceptable latency; speculative warming accepts small mismatch risk.
- Aggressive shedding protects SLOs but raises customer churn risk for non-enterprise tiers; choose tiered policies.

Relevant artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/117642/traffic-divergence-backpressure (confluence link)
- Prototype PR (edge-proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1284
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streams/active-active-handoff-loadtest
acceptance_criteria:
- Handshake protocol implemented and behind feature flag on canary cluster.
- Dual-feed overlap defaults to 250ms and is configurable per-route.
- Circuit breaker fires when queue-depth > 500ms expected wait OR token tail-latency > 1500ms for 30s window.
- Load-shedding enforces tiered thresholds; unit and integration tests cover both preferential and fallback paths.
- Telemetry emitted: per-session-handoff, dual-feed-duration, handoff-success, shed-rate-by-tier; dashboards for runtime-1.22 SLO monitoring created.
- No regressions observed in canary traffic for median latency and error-rate; documented canary sign-off from infra and reliability PMs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: deploy handshake and telemetry in internal staging for synthetic replay (1 week).
Phase 1: enable feature flag for 1% of production traffic in eastus and europe-west for non-critical tiers (2 weeks), monitor SLOs and handoff metrics.
Phase 2: expand to 10% with preferential handling for P0/P1 customers and run chaos test (region failover) during maintenance window.
Phase 3: enable dual-feed for all streaming routes in targeted regions with configurable overlap; run regression telemetry queries.
Phase 4: global enablement and documentation update plus runbook update in incident response.
Rollback: instant feature flag disable; fallback to current sticky-routing where handshake not available.
telemetry_requirements:
Emit metrics with these labels: region, source_region, dest_region, session_id_hash, customer_tier, route, model_variant.
Metrics: handoff_attempts, handoff_successes, dual_feed_ms_histogram, queue_depth_ms, shed_count_by_tier, cb_open_count, session_reconnect_rate.
Traces: sample 1% of handoffs with full span across gateway -> runtime -> model to measure end-to-end impact.
Dashboards: release SLO dashboard and an alert rule: handoff_success_rate < 98% for 10m triggers SEV2.
tasks: Edge proxy: implement handoff token and dual-feed plumbing (PR #1284)
Gateway: queue-based admission controller + client backpressure frames
Runtime: accept warmup tokens and support speculative KV warming
SLO/observability: add metrics, dashboards, and alert rules
Playbook: update regional failover runbook and postmortem checklist
Testing: synthetic replay tests and chaos runbook for region failover
